propositions.text: Mr. Adiele and his minor children seek judicial review of an officer's refusal of his open work permit application.
propositions.quote: Mr. Paul Uchemadu Adiele (the “Principal Applicant”) and his minor children Wisdom Ugonna Adiele-Paul, Miracle Nneoma Adiele-Paul, and Praise Chidera Adiele-Paul (collectively “the Applicants”) seek judicial review of the decision of an officer (the “Officer”) refusing his application for an open work permit

propositions.text: The work permit was to accompany his wife, a student at University of Saskatchewan.
propositions.quote: in order to accompany his wife, a student at the University of Saskatchewan.

paragraphs.summary: The applicants seek judicial review of an officer's refusal of an open work permit to accompany the wife, a student at University of Saskatchewan.

propositions.text: The application was refused on Feb 2, 2024 for insufficient evidence that wife was a full-time student at a DLI.
propositions.quote: The Principal Applicant’s application was refused on February 2, 2024, on the grounds that there was insufficient evidence submitted to show that his wife was a full-time student at a Designated Learning Institution (“DLI”)

paragraphs.summary: The officer refused the application on Feb 2, 2024 due to insufficient evidence of wife's full-time student status at a DLI.

propositions.text: Applicant requested reconsideration on Feb 5, 2024.
propositions.quote: On February 5, 2024, the Principal Applicant requested reconsideration of the decision.

propositions.text: IRCC responded on Feb 7, 2024 acknowledging reconsideration request and stating no response in 10 days means refusal.
propositions.quote: On February 7, 2024, Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canda (“IRCC”) responded to Counsel for the Principal Applicant in the following terms: ... If you do not hear from us in 10 working days, then you should consider your request to have your application reconsidered on the grounds you presented in your request to have been refused.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant requested reconsideration Feb 5; IRCC responded Feb 7 acknowledging request and stating no reply in 10 days means refusal.

propositions.text: Applicant swore affidavit May 19, 2025 stating no further contact from IRCC within 10 days.
propositions.quote: In his Further Affidavit sworn on May 19, 2025, ... he did not hear further from IRCC within 10 days about the reconsideration request.

propositions.text: Applicant filed application for leave and judicial review on Feb 29, 2024 regarding Feb 2 decision.
propositions.quote: He filed his application for leave and judicial review about the February 2, 2024 decision on February 29, 2024.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant swore affidavit May 19, 2025 of no IRCC contact within 10 days; filed judicial review Feb 29, 2024 of Feb 2 decision.

propositions.text: On Oct 21, 2024 IRCC said spouse was full-time student but refused permit based on funds.
propositions.quote: On October 21, 2024, IRCC sent the Principal Applicant an email advising ... application for an open work permit “remains refused based on funds”.

paragraphs.summary: IRCC emailed Oct 21, 2024 confirming spouse's full-time student status but refused permit due to insufficient funds.

propositions.text: Respondent objected to inclusion in Certified Tribunal Record of reconsideration materials.
propositions.quote: The Minister of Citizenship and Immigration (the “Respondent”) objected to the inclusion in that CTR of materials relating to the Principal Applicant’s request for reconsideration of the February 2, 2024 decision.

paragraphs.summary: Respondent objected to including reconsideration materials in the Certified Tribunal Record.

propositions.text: An amended Certified Tribunal Record was filed excluding reconsideration materials.
propositions.quote: An amended CTR was filed on November 7, 2024, excluding materials about the reconsideration request.

paragraphs.summary: An amended Certified Tribunal Record was filed Nov 7, 2024 excluding reconsideration materials.

propositions.text: Order granting leave was issued April 16, 2025.
propositions.quote: The Order granting leave in this matter was issued on April 16, 2025.

paragraphs.summary: Order granting leave was issued April 16, 2025.

propositions.text: Applicant argues Feb 2 decision about wife's student status is unreasonable and should be set aside.
propositions.quote: The Principal Applicant now argues that the decision of the Officer about his wife’s status as a full-time student is unreasonable because it was made without regard to the evidence and should be set aside.

propositions.text: Applicant submits Officer breached procedural fairness by denying opportunity to address funds issue in Oct 21 decision.
propositions.quote: He also submits that the Officer breached the duty of procedural fairness by depriving him of the opportunity to address the question of sufficient funds, when making the decision on October 21, 2024.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues Feb 2 decision unreasonable and Officer breached procedural fairness on funds issue in Oct 21 decision.

propositions.text: Respondent submits judicial review is moot as reconsideration decision on Oct 21 was refused and no review filed.
propositions.quote: The Respondent submits that the application for judicial review is moot, since the application for an open work permit was reconsidered and refused on October 21, 2024 and no application for leave and judicial review was filed in respect of that decision.

paragraphs.summary: Respondent submits judicial review is moot because reconsideration decision was refused and no review filed.

propositions.text: Procedural fairness issues are reviewed on correctness standard, citing Khosa.
propositions.quote: Any issue of procedural fairness is reviewable on the standard of correctness; see the decision in Canada (Citizenship and Immigration) v Khosa, [2009] 1 S.C.R. 339.

paragraphs.summary: Procedural fairness issues are reviewed on correctness standard, citing Khosa.

propositions.text: Merits of decision are reviewed on reasonableness standard per Vavilov.
propositions.quote: Following the decision of the Supreme Court of Canada in Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration) v. Vavilov, [2019] 4 S.C.R. 653, the merits of the decision are reviewable on the standard of reasonableness.

paragraphs.summary: Merits of decision are reviewed on reasonableness standard per Vavilov.

propositions.text: Reasonableness requires justification, transparency, intelligibility, and relation to factual and legal constraints per Vavilov.
propositions.quote: In considering reasonableness, the Court is to ask if the decision under review "bears the hallmarks of reasonableness — justification, transparency and intelligibility — and whether it is justified in relation to the relevant factual and legal constraints that bear on that decision"; see Vavilov, supra at paragraph 99.

paragraphs.summary: Reasonableness requires justification, transparency, intelligibility, and relation to factual and legal constraints per Vavilov.

propositions.text: Applicant seeks orders quashing refusal and inadmissibility decisions, directing grant or redetermination, and further orders.
propositions.quote: In his application, the Principal Applicant seeks the following relief: a) An Order quashing the decision refusing the Applicant’s application pursuant to Immigration and Refugee Protection Act; b) An Order quashing the decision finding the Applicant inadmissible to Canada the pursuant to Immigration and Refugee Protection Act; and b)[sic] An Order directing an officer at the High Commission of Canada, Visa /Study Permit Section, Kenya, to grant the Applicant’s application pursuant to Immigration and Refugee Protection Act; or in the alternative c) An Order referring the matter to another Officer of Citizenship and Immigration Canada, High Commission of Canada, Visa /Study Permit Section, Kenya for re-determination by a different Officer in accordance with the law. d) Such further Orders as this Honourable Court allows.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant seeks orders quashing refusal and inadmissibility decisions, directing grant or redetermination, and further orders.

propositions.text: Borowski sets two-step mootness test: live controversy and discretion to hear moot case considering adversarial context, judicial economy, and court role.
propositions.quote: The leading authority on mootness is the Supreme Court of Canada’s decision in Borowski v. Canada (Attorney General), 1989 CanLII 123 (S.C.C.), [1989] 1 S.C.R. 342 (Borowski). Borowski sets out a two-step analysis to determine whether a case is moot and, in the affirmative, whether a court should nonetheless exercise its discretion to hear it. ... The second step of the analysis involves consideration of three factors: the presence of an adversarial context, the concern for judicial economy, and the need for the court to be sensitive to its role as the adjudicative branch in our political framework.

paragraphs.summary: Borowski sets two-step mootness test: live controversy and discretion to hear moot case considering adversarial context, judicial economy, and court role.

propositions.text: Application of mootness principle is discretionary for the court.
propositions.quote: I observe that application of the principle of mootness is a discretionary decision by a Court.

paragraphs.summary: Application of mootness principle is discretionary for the court.

propositions.text: Respondent did not raise mootness at leave stage but did so in Further Memorandum.
propositions.quote: In his Memorandum of argument filed at the leave stage, the Respondent did not raise the issue of mootness. He raised the issue in his Further Memorandum.

paragraphs.summary: Respondent raised mootness issue only in Further Memorandum, not at leave stage.

propositions.text: Revised Certified Tribunal Record excludes reconsideration decision but it is attached as exhibit to applicant's Further affidavit.
propositions.quote: The revised CTR does not contain the reconsideration decision, but it is attached as an exhibit to the Further affidavit filed by the Principal Applicant.

propositions.text: Respondent did not object to inclusion of reconsideration decision exhibit.
propositions.quote: The Respondent did not object to the inclusion of the exhibit.

paragraphs.summary: Revised record excludes reconsideration decision but applicant attached it; respondent did not object to exhibit inclusion.

propositions.text: Reconsideration decision does not identify decision-maker; basis of respondent's mootness argument.
propositions.quote: The “reconsideration” decision does not identify the decision-maker, whether it was the Officer or someone else. This decision is the basis of the Respondent’s argument about mootness.

paragraphs.summary: Reconsideration decision lacks decision-maker ID; respondent bases mootness argument on it.

propositions.text: Court declines to dismiss application on grounds of mootness, exercising discretion.
propositions.quote: In this case, I decline to dismiss this application on the grounds of mootness.

paragraphs.summary: Court declines to dismiss application on mootness grounds, exercising discretion.

propositions.text: A live controversy remains between the parties regarding the application for an open work permit.
propositions.quote: a “live controversy” remains between the parties, that is the application for an open work permit

propositions.text: It is not necessary to address other elements of the mootness discussion.
propositions.quote: It is not necessary for me to address the other elements of the mootness discussion.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds a live controversy remains about the open work permit application and declines to address mootness further.

propositions.text: The decision of February 2, 2024 was made without regard to the evidence and fails the reasonableness standard.
propositions.quote: the decision of February 2, 2024 was made without regard to the evidence. This means that the decision fails to meet the standard of reasonableness.

propositions.text: The applicants submitted that the February 2, 2024 decision was made without regard to the evidence and was unreasonable.
propositions.quote: I agree with the submissions of the Applicants, that the decision of February 2, 2024 was made without regard to the evidence.

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees with the applicants that the February 2, 2024 decision was unreasonable and ignored evidence.

propositions.text: It is unnecessary to address procedural fairness and the argument is not properly raised in this judicial review application.
propositions.quote: It is not necessary for me to address the issue of procedural fairness. In any event, this argument is not appropriately raised in the within application for judicial review.

paragraphs.summary: The court declines to address procedural fairness, finding the argument improperly raised in this judicial review.

propositions.text: The application for judicial review is granted, the decision is set aside, and the matter is remitted to a different officer for redetermination.
propositions.quote: The application for judicial review will be granted, the decision will be set aside and the matter will be remitted to a different officer for re-determination.

propositions.text: There is no question for certification.
propositions.quote: There is no question for certification.

paragraphs.summary: The court grants judicial review, sets aside the decision, remits the matter to another officer, and finds no question for certification.
